notes: 4-page 'Proforma Invoice' wholesale order with a dense multi-column item table (Code/Description/Qty/Price/Amount/GST). PyMuPDF's text-layer reading order breaks each table row into separate per-cell lines, so line items and (legitimately) the invoice number are not recoverable by this tier -- it uses 'Ref:' instead of a labelled invoice number, and has no explicit currency code (it's an Australian document with no AUD/RM token anywhere in the text). Header fields that ARE clearly labelled ('Doc Date:', 'GRAND TOTAL:') are correctly found. This is the intended hard-case example: a real document where Tier 2 gets the header right but line items wrong, which the gate currently still accepts on header strength alone -- a good case to revisit once Tier 3 table-structure models exist.
